newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan vice-minister, delegation leave for China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan vice-minister, delegation leave for China.

text.p: A group of Taiwanese officials and scholars left for China on Sunday to promote education exchanges despite the political stalemate between the two rivals, local media said.

Yang Chao-hsiang, vice-minister of Taiwan's education ministry, and an 18-member delegation of officials and scholars would visit universities and cultural establishments in Beijing, Shanghai, Nanjing and Xian, the reports said.
They were expected to meet Wang Zhaoguo, director of the State Council's Taiwan Affairs Office and Tang Shubei, Beijing's negotiator with Taipei, during the 12-day visit.
Yang and other officials would travel in a private capacity, the reports said.
The group is scheduled to return to the island on October 31.
Taiwan has banned all direct official contact with China since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949. Beijing regards Taipei as a renegade province.

Despite the ban, indirect economic and cultural exchanges have flourished since the late 1980s when political tensions started to thaw. About 30,000 Taiwan companies have invested more than US$20 billion in China.
A group of business leaders from China, led by Guo Dongpo, the chairman of China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, is presently visiting the island.
